title: Fewest Brackets to Balance
statement:
You get a string s made only of '(' and ')'. You may insert brackets anywhere, but never delete or move existing ones.

Return the fewest insertions needed to make the string balanced: every '(' is later closed by its own ')', and no ')' appears without an open '(' before it.

examples.why: The counts are equal, but order matters: the two leading ')' need two '(' in front, and the two trailing '(' need two ')' after.
One '(' is matched; the other two are still open at the end, so add "))" in the right places.
Only the first ')' has nothing to close. One '(' at the start fixes it.

hints: Comparing the number of '(' and ')' is not enough. Example 1 has equal counts but needs four insertions.
Read left to right and keep the number of brackets that are open right now. What does it mean when a ')' arrives and that number is 0?
That ')' can only be fixed by inserting a '(' before it, so count one insertion. At the end, every bracket still open needs one ')' inserted.

explain.intuition:
Matching brackets is a stack problem, but the stack only ever holds '(', so its size is all you need: a counter of brackets that are open right now, just like a nesting depth counter.

Two things can go wrong. A ')' may arrive when nothing is open; nothing later can fix it, so you must insert a '(' before it and count one. And when the string ends, every bracket still open needs its own ')'. The answer is the sum of those two counts, and each insertion fixes exactly one problem, so you cannot do better.
steps: For ')': if open > 0, decrement it; otherwise increment added (an inserted '(' pairs with it).
pitfalls: Returning |count('(') − count(')')|. It ignores order, so "))((" would get 0.
Letting open go negative and then returning |open| at the end. A later '(' would cancel an earlier unmatched ')', which is not allowed.
Forgetting the brackets still open at the end.

solutions.title: Erase matched pairs until none are left
solutions.idea: Every adjacent "()" is a matched pair; delete pairs repeatedly. Whatever remains is unmatched and needs one insertion each.

solutions.title: Open counter
solutions.idea: Count brackets open right now. A ')' with nothing open needs an inserted '('; whatever is still open at the end needs a ')'.

followups: Return one balanced string of minimum length that you get by inserting, not just the count.
The string also has '[' and ']', which must nest correctly with '(' and ')'. Is a counter still enough?
lcTitle: Minimum Add to Make Parentheses Valid
